**Clinical Summary:**  
A 20–40-year-old male presents with persistent, minimally pressure-responsive gingival bleeding following third molar extraction. Hemophilia B (factor IX) and severe von Willebrand disease (particularly type 3 or 2N) remain differential considerations. Early diagnosis enables prophylactic therapy, prevention of hemarthroses and chronic arthropathy, and informed family planning. Genetic testing and cascade screening of at-risk male relatives (e.g., brothers, sons) and carrier testing for female relatives are indicated upon confirmation.
